speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn with increasing yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin; have you noticed if this yellowing started right after birth or if it has been getting worse over the last few days?

When did you first notice the jaundice, and has your baby been feeding well or having normal wet diapers?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-week-old female newborn. The patient has been experiencing increasing yellow discoloration of her eyes and skin for 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation, initially weighed 3066 g and now weighs 3200 g. The patient is exclusively breastfed.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Jaundice (Breastfeeding Jaundice). Given the age of 2 weeks, exclusive breastfeeding, and lack of other risk factors like hemolysis or infection, this is most consistent with suboptimal intake leading to dehydration and delayed stooling, rather than pathologic hyperbilirubinemia requiring immediate phototherapy. I will recommend a Bilirubin Level test to confirm the severity and guide management. REQUEST TEST: Total_Serum_Bilirubin.
